Pathway map

No proposed route runs from raw materials to self-copying RNA

We wrote four proposed routes as step tables, straight from the papers, and scored every hand-off with a rule we sealed before we started. A step counts as joined only if it can run on what the step before left behind, using a named physical process.

02First breaks

Two routes break before their first step, two right after it

  1. Cyanosulfidic

    Breaks after step 1

    The sugars come out trapped as oxazolidinones (Ritson 2012), and the next step needs free glycolaldehyde. It still gets furthest, to short RNA chains, but 8 of its 9 hand-offs are unexplained.

  2. Alkaline vent

    Breaks after step 1

    Formate and acetate form across iron-sulfide walls (Altair 2025). No vent step to sugars or nucleotides has been published.

  3. Warm pond

    Breaks before step 1

    The pond has no nucleotide source. Both pond papers start from laboratory nucleotides.

  4. Ice and RNA

    Breaks before step 1

    Nothing makes the triplet building blocks, and every RNA input, the ribozyme included, is supplied purified.

The alkaline vent ranks first by the rule, with no hard fail. That is an artefact: 5 of its 6 steps have no published chemistry, so there is nothing to break.

03Top gaps

Sustained replication is missing from every route

No route has any published step in which a replicator makes more copies of itself than it loses. The only template copying with a yield uses a purified, selected ribozyme with purified triplets, primers and a hexamer.

04The rule

Nine hard fails decide whether a hand-off breaks

Step k+1 may use what step k leaves only through named physical processes from a closed list of 14, such as drying, heating, mixing or thermophoresis. The rule was hashed before any route was encoded, and it caught all 28 planted test cases first.

The rule and its planted control

Hard fails

  • F1 pH
  • F2 temperature
  • F3 solvent
  • F4 input source
  • F5 concentration
  • F6 purified hand-off
  • F7 process validity
  • F8 redox
  • F9 setting

Warnings

  • W1 untested interference
  • W2 thin concentration
  • W3 claimed separation

05Literature view

The literature runs further, to compartments and evolution, but with gaps at every stage

These statuses come from the literature and cover the whole path to evolution. The scored map above covers the first five stages, under the compatibility rule hashed in advance.

StepBest evidenceStatus
Feedstocks (HCN, formaldehyde, phosphate, sulfides) in a stated settingSeveral settings proposed; each supplies a different subset.Partial
Amino acids and nucleobasesMade in many routes; 33 amino acids and all five nucleobases in Bennu (2025); all five nucleobases in Ryugu (2026).Met
Ribose and nucleotidesRibose found in Bennu, deoxyribose not (Furukawa et al. 2025); pyrimidine nucleotides (C and U only) made without free ribose (Powner et al. 2009).Partial
Activation (energy-carrying building blocks)Thioester routes in water at neutral pH (Singh et al. 2025).Partial
Polymers long enough to foldShown with purified inputs. Wet-dry cycling gives short mixed RNA chains without activators, 0.1% reaching 10 letters (Caimi et al. 2025); continuity unscored.Partial
Template copyingQT45 copies itself and its complement in ice at about 0.2% yield in 72 days (2026).Partial
Exponential self-replicationShort RNA duplexes, including a ribozyme fragment, replicated exponentially from supplied triplets under freeze-thaw cycles (Attwater et al. 2025); never a whole replicator from scenario feedstocks.Not met
Compartments that grow and divide with their contentsPeptide sequence sets vesicle growth rate (Baba et al. 2026); membranes formed without a parent membrane, using enzymes (Khanal et al. 2026). Growth and division coupled to contents not shown.Partial
Darwinian evolutionRNA-catalysed evolution of a catalytic RNA (Papastavrou, Horning & Joyce, PNAS 2024), not open-ended.Not met

Scenarios

Alkaline hydrothermal vents

Explains a natural energy source (pH gradients) and CO2 reduction to formate and acetate.

Cannot yet anything beyond two-carbon products; nucleotides.

Surface ponds with wet-dry cycles

Explains concentration and joining of nucleotides by drying, without added activators.

Cannot yet chains stay short as breakdown balances growth; some natural spring waters destroy RNA.

Cyanosulfidic surface chemistry

Explains common origins for nucleotide, amino acid and lipid precursors under UV light.

Cannot yet its sugars come out trapped, and no named process frees them; no canonical purines.

Ice (eutectic freezing)

Explains concentrates RNA and slows breakdown; QT45 works here.

Cannot yet where the activated triplets come from.
